expected.description:
BOMBANANA! is a chaotic, explosively funny co-op multiplayer game for three, where each player has only part of the information - blind monkey, deaf monkey and mute monkey must work together to defuse a bomb, or everyone goes BOOM! Will your friendship survive the ultimate test?

MEET YOUR SQUAD!🙈 Blind Monkey: You can’t see the bomb, but you can touch the bomb! 👍 Sadly, you can’t see colors or read screens. You’ll need to rely on your teammates for the rest. 

🙊 Mute Monkey: You are the only one who can read the bomb disposal manual. If only you could tell the others what you know.

 

🙉 Deaf Monkey: You can see the bomb and you can see your friends as they frantically gesture at you. Sadly, you can’t hear a thing, but at this point, would you even want to?

As you gamble with your friends' lives, you must rely on each other and your monkeys' unique abilities. Communication is key, and there’s no one right way to defuse the bomb. We don’t impose any methods: wave, shout, throw bananas. Working out how you communicate is your job.

WARNING!Players can and should expect peak amounts of misunderstanding, unjust accusations, and desperate body language, placing your friendships in jeopardy. Just because you keep talking, that doesn't mean nobody explodes. Even if you manage to survive the bomb, there's no guarantee your friendship will. Some might call this game "friendslop". We disagree. If anything, it's a new genre: anti-friendslop, or perhaps an argument simulator. 🤔

We’ll let you be the judge!

FEATURES!3-Player Co-op - No more, no less. Exactly three monkeys required

3 Game Modes -

Campaign - 30 handcrafted levels with increasing difficulty

Endless - Procedurally generated, wave-based levels that keep getting harder

Custom - Players create their own challenge by adjusting bomb difficulty, the timer, module types, environmental hazards, and how many mistakes are allowed

Asymmetric Roles - Every player sees, hears, and acts differently

Fun interactions - Point, wave, gesture or flail wildly. Your options are only limited by your imagination and each player's Emote wheel

Slapping - Obviously an essential feature

New Environments: We all know the trusty minivan, but what about a plane? What other environments can you defuse bombs in?

Environmental Hazards: Navigate events like power outages, obstructions and loud interruptions

Voice Chat - Some of you can talk, some of you can’t. You’ll figure it out

Puzzle Modules - Each bomb has different modules and different rules, all of which are guaranteed to induce different kinds of panic

Level System - Defuse the bomb to unlock new levels. The better you get, the harder they are

Color Blind Mode - Just because the monkey is blind, doesn’t mean he can’t defuse a bomb! Colors used across objects and the UI have been adapted to support two different types of color blindness.

installSteps.text: Alternatively, download BOMBANANA! directly from the official site at http://bombanana.leftostudio.com/. Always download from the official source — third-party mirrors of free games are a common malware vector.
BOMBANANA! is also on Steam and is free there. Open the store page and press Play Game to add it to your library.

Run the downloaded installer and follow the prompts. If Windows SmartScreen warns about an unrecognised publisher, that is normal for open-source projects without a paid code-signing certificate — choose More info, then Run anyway.
Open the downloaded .dmg and drag the app into Applications. On first launch macOS may refuse to open it as unidentified — right-click the app and choose Open to approve it once.
Launch the game and look at the settings menu before your first session — resolution and control defaults are worth checking. BOMBANANA! needs roughly 300 MB of free disk space.

set.tagline: Three monkeys, one bomb, and nobody has enough senses to explain the problem.
set.description: Lefto Studio's three-player online co-op puzzle game gives each monkey a different piece of the bomb-disposal problem. One sees, one touches, one reads the manual; everyone has to find a way to communicate before the timer runs out.

qualityBar.verdict: The bomb is simple compared with the conversation required to tell your friends where it is.

set.longDescription:
BOMBANANA! gives three friends a bomb and refuses to give any one of them the whole picture. The blind monkey can handle the device but cannot read its colors or displays. The deaf monkey sees the bomb and everyone waving at it but cannot hear the shouted plan. The mute monkey can read the manual and cannot simply tell the others what it says. You are left to invent a language fast enough to beat the timer.

That arrangement makes communication the game, not just something you do between puzzles. A correct observation can be useless if the person who needs it cannot hear you. A good instruction can turn into frantic pointing across the room. The slapstick comes from these mismatched roles rather than from random chaos. When a team finally develops a workable routine, the next module or environmental hazard can break it. You may learn as much about your friends' patience as you do about bomb wiring.

Lefto Studio built three modes around the same three-person requirement. The campaign has 30 handcrafted levels; Endless builds waves that keep increasing the pressure; Custom lets a group adjust difficulty, timing, modules, hazards and allowed mistakes. Steam says exactly three players are required, no more and no fewer. That is a real constraint for a party invitation. The game offers an in-game server browser and room codes, so friends can get into the same session without PlayBound hosting a dedicated server. We have not verified an automatic PlayBound party handoff; the room code remains the reliable join method for this Draft listing.

The game is sold on Steam for Windows and macOS. It is not a free direct download, even though the previous PlayBound steps said to press Play Game on a supposedly free Steam page. We corrected that route without changing any stored prices. The developer's FAQ confirms Xbox, PlayStation DualSense/DualShock 4 and generic XInput controller support, so the controller badge is native rather than an untested PlayBound remap. Steam publishes separate Windows and Mac hardware requirements; Mac needs more storage but less RAM at the stated minimum, a distinction the old page missed. Every player needs broadband and their own game copy for online co-op.

We like BOMBANANA! because its joke is also its rule set. One friend cannot solve the bomb while the others watch, and three people cannot brute-force a language they have not invented yet. The best moments are probably not the clean defusals. They are the seconds after someone realizes that the person doing the pointing has been pointing at the wrong thing all along.
set.whyWePickedIt: BOMBANANA! makes cooperation tangible: three roles, three sets of information, and no spare player who can solve it alone. Room codes make it practical for friends to meet online, and the campaign, Endless and Custom modes give the communication puzzle several shapes.
set.thatOneThing: The only monkey with the manual cannot speak, and the only monkey touching the bomb cannot read it. Good luck with your briefing.

installSteps.text: Purchase BOMBANANA! on Steam and install it from your Steam library on a Windows 10/11 64-bit PC. Every participant needs their own copy.
Purchase BOMBANANA! on Steam and install it from your Steam library on macOS 11 or newer. The developer lists a 600 MB minimum for Mac.
Launch the game, choose a supported controller or mouse and keyboard, and arrange exactly three players before creating an online room.

firstPlaySteps.text: Choose one of the three roles, agree on how to communicate information that your role cannot speak, hear or see, and begin with the campaign before adjusting Custom difficulty.

multiplayerGamingSteps.text: One player creates a room in BOMBANANA!, then shares its room code. The other two use the game's server browser or code entry to join. Exactly three players are required.

PlayBound has not verified automatic room-code handoff or a dedicated server for this Draft game. Use the game's own online lobby and keep voice or another communication channel available for the roles that can hear and speak.

faq.a: No. Steam lists it as a paid Windows and Mac game. The old PlayBound Draft install step incorrectly called it free.

faq.q: How many friends do I need?
faq.a: The developer specifies exactly three players in a co-op session. Each person has a different information and communication role.
Yes. The developer's FAQ names Xbox, PlayStation DualSense/DualShock 4 and generic XInput controllers.

faq.q: How do we join each other?
faq.a: Use the in-game server browser or share a room code. PlayBound has not verified automatic lobby joining for this Draft entry.

faq.q: Does PlayBound host a server for it?
faq.a: No verified dedicated-server package is available; the game uses its own online room system.

bestFor: Exactly three friends ready to communicate through deliberately awkward roles
Groups that like co-op puzzles whose answer depends on explaining the problem
notFor: Solo players or groups of two or four who cannot fill exactly three seats
Anyone expecting a free download or a PlayBound-hosted dedicated server
